basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 20.' and it opens 'Vers. 20. Super Ismael quoque exaudivi te. Diximus superius Ismaele Judaeos significari'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 20. Super Ismael quoque exaudivi te. Diximus superius Ismaele Judaeos significari qui aucti | sunt carnali generatione in immensam multitudinem. Unde per prophetam dicitur: Gloria ejus ab utero, et vulva et a conceptu (Ose. IX, 11).-- Duodecim duces generabit. Id est duodecim apostolos, maximos duces Ecclesiae, qui ex illo populo nati sunt. Vel duodecim duces dicit duodecim ipsius populi tribus.
